title: Ode to Joy (theme, arranged for beginners)
subtitle: Theme from Symphony No. 9, simple two-hand arrangement
trains: A simple stepwise melody with steady quarter notes over static left-hand chords - an easy introduction to playing both hands together.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Beethoven, "Ode to Joy" theme (Symphony No. 9, 4th movement; public domain). The melody was checked note by note against the Soprano of the Mutopia Project's public-domain hymn setting (piece-info id 528, ode.ly, typeset by Peter Chubb), transposed from G to C major; the audit record content/library/audit/repertoire/beginner/ode-to-joy.json re-runs that check.
provenance.note: The first two 4-bar phrases only, ending on the tonic; not the complete theme. Bars 4 and 8 keep Beethoven's dotted figure (dotted quarter, eighth, half).

departures: Only the first two phrases (8 bars) of the theme; the middle phrase and the return are left out.
Key: C major (Beethoven's theme is in D major; the hymn setting it was checked against is in G major).
Left hand: our own block chords, one or two per bar (I, V, IV), instead of Beethoven's orchestra.
